_about: English strings for the site (site/i18n/README in docs/dev/website.md). Keys are grouped by page; {name} placeholders are filled in by the generator or the scripts.
nav.label: Main
home.title: Firmware for DMR radios
home.headline: Open firmware for DMR radios
home.lead: MIT-licensed firmware for Baofeng, TYT and Radioddity DMR radios. One source tree for every radio.
home.p1_text: DMR Tier II and analog FM. CTCSS/DCS, VOX, scan, dual watch, VFO.
home.p2_text: Text messages, ARS, LRRP location, emergency, call alert, radio check. IP over DMR.
home.p3_text: MMDVM hotspot, single frequency repeater, split duplex. USB network: status page, rigctld, SNMP, TFTP. APRS.
home.p4_text: Web flasher with backup and restore, or the odrflash command line tool. The codec comes from your radio or your stock firmware file.
status.testing: Builds, not on a radio yet
radios.title: Radios
radios.lead: Supported and planned radios, generated from the repository.
radio.description: OpenDigitalRadio on the {name}: status, features, screens, installing.
radio.image_note: Click a screen below to show it here.
radio.screens_lead: Rendered by the firmware's UI code at this radio's resolution. Screens for features the radio lacks are left out.
radio.features_lead: Features per variant on this radio.
radio.flash_soon: Not in the web flasher yet. See the documentation below.

features.variants_lead: Prebuilt sets of switches. The flasher shows the differences feature by feature.

tools.convert_text: Identifies a codeplug file and lists the available conversions.
tools.contacts_text: DMR ID database from public sources, filtered by country or network.
tools.editor_text: Channels, zones and contacts, written to the radio over USB.
tools.convert.none: No conversion for this format yet.

flash.title: Install and back up
flash.lead: Back up, install and restore over USB. Needs Chrome, Edge or another Chromium browser on a computer.
radios.list_lead: Sorted by status. Planned radios need hardware on the bench before a port starts.
flash.start.title: Task
flash.start.lead: Every step is shown before anything is written.
flash.task.install.text: Install or update OpenDigitalRadio. Includes a backup.
flash.task.backup.text: Firmware, codeplug and calibration of a radio running OpenDigitalRadio.
flash.task.restore.text: From a backup file made here: back to the backed-up state, or back to stock firmware.
flash.start.privacy: Firmware images come from this site. Your stock firmware file, backups and radio data stay on your computer.
flash.support.none: This browser can't reach a radio (no WebUSB or Web Serial). Use Chrome, Edge or another Chromium browser on a computer.
flash.support.usb: This browser can't reach the radio's bootloader (no WebUSB). Use Chrome, Edge or another Chromium browser on a computer.
flash.support.serial: This browser can't talk to a radio running OpenDigitalRadio (no Web Serial). Use Chrome, Edge or another Chromium browser on a computer.
flash.sim.banner: Simulated radio: nothing here touches real hardware. Use it to try the steps.
flash.sim.try: Try it with a simulated radio
flash.sim.image: The simulation writes a made-up firmware image.
flash.sim.enter_bootloader: Simulate: put the radio in its bootloader
flash.radio.title: Which radio?
flash.radio.lead: Pick your radio. Radios the flasher can't write yet are grayed out; their pages explain how to install today.
flash.radio.not_yet: Not in the web flasher yet
flash.radio.detect_hint: Connect the radio with its programming cable and turn it on normally. Radios on stock firmware can't be detected; pick yours above.
flash.build.title: Pick your build
flash.build.lead: Start from a prebuilt variant. Open “Customize” to see every feature and change any of them.
flash.build.customize: Customize: every feature, à la carte
flash.build.custom_diff: {added} added, {removed} removed compared with the variant
flash.build.custom_text: This combination isn't prebuilt. Build it with the command below (docs: Building), then load the image here. A build service may come later.
flash.build.will_download: Release {version} ({size} KB) is downloaded from this site and checked before anything is written.
flash.build.no_release_text: No release image for this radio and variant is on the site yet. Developers can load their own build below.
flash.build.own_text: An image you built (build/<radio>/odr_<radio>.bin), with its release manifest (.json) if you have one.
flash.now.title: What runs on your radio now?
flash.now.lead: This decides how the codec is handled and what can be backed up first.
flash.now.odr_text: Turn the radio on normally and connect it: the flasher asks it directly.
flash.now.stock_text: The firmware the radio came with.
flash.now.unknown_text: The codec is then written from your stock firmware file.
flash.now.which_version: Stock firmware version (shown at power-on or in the radio's menu):
flash.now.stock_backup_later: Stock firmware can't be read over USB on this radio. After OpenDigitalRadio is on the radio, the flasher reads its memory, including your stock codeplug and calibration, and saves the backup. Flashing never touches that memory.
flash.now.stock_backup_planned: Reading stock firmware directly is planned for this radio. For now the backup is taken right after the install, before anything else changes.
flash.backup.title: Back up first
flash.backup.lead: Save what the radio holds before it changes. The file stays on your computer.
flash.backup.after_lead: OpenDigitalRadio is running, so the radio's memory can be read now. It still holds your stock codeplug and calibration. Save it before you change anything.
flash.backup.full_text: Internal flash, the whole 16 MB memory chip and the factory calibration. A few minutes.
flash.backup.quick_text: Internal flash, the codeplug area and calibration. Faster, but stock firmware resources aren't kept.
flash.backup.saved: Backup saved ({size} KB). Keep it somewhere safe.
flash.backup.incomplete: Some reads ended early: {files}. The backup is saved, but restore can't use those parts.
flash.backup.note_after: Taken right after OpenDigitalRadio was installed over stock firmware: the memory chip was not yet changed.
flash.backup.task_lead: Turn the radio on normally with OpenDigitalRadio running and connect it.
flash.backup.add_stock: Add your stock firmware file to the backup (lets restore put stock firmware back)
flash.backup.stock_none: A radio on stock firmware can't be backed up here. Use Install: the backup is taken right after OpenDigitalRadio is on the radio.
flash.codec.title: The codec
flash.codec.lead: DMR voice needs the radio maker's AMBE codec. It isn't part of OpenDigitalRadio: it either stays in your radio or comes from your own stock firmware file.
flash.codec.mode.keep: Keep the codec in the radio
flash.codec.mode.merge: Write the codec from your stock file
flash.codec.stock_needed: Needed: the radio's bootloader key and (when writing the codec) the codec come from it. Supported: {files}.
flash.codec.stock_optional: Optional here: the key is remembered on this computer. Supported codec source: {files}.
flash.write.title: Write the firmware
flash.write.bootloader_title: Put the radio in its bootloader
flash.write.windows_hint: Windows: the bootloader needs the WinUSB driver, installed once with Zadig (pick “STM32 BOOTLOADER”).
flash.write.unexpected: The bootloader reports “{what}”, which isn't what this radio's bootloader shows. Check you picked the right radio.
flash.write.failed: Writing stopped: {error}. The bootloader is never erased: put the radio back in its bootloader and write again.
flash.done.title: Check the radio
flash.done.lead: The radio restarts into OpenDigitalRadio. Wait for the screen, then connect it to check the codec.
flash.done.no_codec: The radio has no usable codec: DMR voice is off, FM works. Go back and write the codec from your stock file.
flash.restore.title: Choose your backup file
flash.restore.lead: A backup bundle (.zip) saved by this flasher.
flash.restore.to_odr_text: The firmware and codec as they were, then the codeplug.
flash.restore.to_stock_text: The manufacturer's firmware from your stock file, codec included.
flash.restore.stock_needed: Choose the stock firmware file: it holds the firmware to write back and the bootloader key.
flash.restore.done_stock: The radio restarts on its stock firmware.
flash.restore.spi_note: The memory chip (codeplug, calibration) was left as it is. If you changed the codeplug under OpenDigitalRadio, write your stock codeplug with the manufacturer's programming software. Writing the whole memory chip back from the backup needs a firmware feature that is planned.
flash.restore.codeplug_lead: When the radio has restarted, connect it: the flasher compares its codeplug with the backup and writes back what differs.
flash.restore.codeplug_refused: {n} of {total} sectors were refused by the radio (areas it protects).
flash.err.load: The flasher's data didn't load. Reload the page.
flash.err.security: The browser blocked USB access. The page must be opened over https or localhost.
flash.err.no_serial: This browser has no Web Serial.
flash.err.no_answer: The radio didn't answer. Is it on and running OpenDigitalRadio? Another program may have its port open.
flash.err.wrong_board: The radio says it is a {board}, not a {name}.
flash.err.not_in_bootloader: The radio isn't in its bootloader.
flash.err.need_stock_for_key: Choose your stock firmware file first: the bootloader key is derived from it.
flash.err.stock_as_image: That's a stock firmware file, not an OpenDigitalRadio image.
flash.net.check: Radio not in the list? Check for USB network mode
flash.net.found: The radio is in USB network mode: it has no serial port, so the flasher can't reach it.
flash.net.none: No radio in USB network mode found either. Check the cable and that the radio is on and running OpenDigitalRadio.
flash.net.step1: On the radio: Tools > USB network (OK, 5, 4), choose “Switch USB to serial”.
flash.net.step2: If Settings > Connections > USB network at start is on, turn it off, or the radio starts as a network adapter again.
flash.net.why: In network mode the radio's tools are on UDP port 3334, which a web page can't use.
